Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase! The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan walk in swinging their swords for Pakistan. Kwena Maphaka has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. There is a bit of delay as Rizwan is unhappy with a light flickering beside the sightscreen. All fine now and we are good to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Now, with the stage set, it’s over to Pakistan for their reply. Will they chase down the target or will South Africa’s bowlers rise to the occasion? Stay tuned, folks, it’s going to be an exciting second half...

On the bowling front, Pakistan had their moments. While Abrar Ahmed’s spell was somewhat expensive, he did manage to snare three crucial wickets. Shaheen Afridi, however, was the standout, as he picked up three vital wickets as well, including that of the in-form Miller, while maintaining a tight economy rate. One can’t help but wonder, had Miller been dismissed early, and George Linde on time, South Africa’s total might have looked very different indeed. Also, in a surprising turn of events, Pakistan were outstanding with their fielding, which is often a point of critique for their team.

Despite losing wickets at regular intervals, Miller single-handedly lifted South Africa from a precarious position. His dismissal in the 14th over was a significant moment, as it subdued the scoring rate considerably. The remaining batters were left with the challenging task of finishing strong but George Linde stood up at that moment to play an explosive knock at the end. He fell on the last ball with just two runs shy of his half-century, giving his team an upper hand!

A first half, slightly in favour of the hosts as they end up with a score of 183 on the board! They faced an uphill battle after losing three early wickets. Enter David Miller, the man of the hour, who truly took the Pakistan bowlers to task. He ran havoc over the Pakistan bowlers with his 82 runs off just 40 balls and kept the scoreboard ticking with his barrage of boundaries, sending several balls into the stands.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! George Linde holes out on the last ball of the innings! He has done his job though. His 48 off 24 balls has helped South Africa finish with 183. Coming to the delivery, this was bowled slower through the air and the length was pulled back a bit, outside off, George Linde attempted the slog sweep as he reached out in front. Got more height than distance on it. Irfan Khan settled under it and did the rest at deep mid-wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: Full, on off, Heinrich Klaasen taps it to the left of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Abbas Afridi to Heinrich Klaasen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh! Length in the channel and this one shapes away late. Heinrich Klaasen has a lazy waft at it and is beaten all ends up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Abbas Afridi to Heinrich Klaasen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be pace from both ends as Abbas Afridi comes on to bowl.
Length again, on off, David Miller turns it through square leg for a brace. A shaky start from South Africa but these two need to steady the ship now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Haris Rauf to David Miller, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Shout for lbw, not given! On a length and just down leg, David Miller looks to flick it but gets a blow on his pads. A loud appeal but the finger stays down. Mohammad Rizwan has a chat with Haris Rauf and they decide not to review it. Good decision though, as it looked to be missing leg!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Haris Rauf to David Miller, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller this time, targeting the stumps, David Miller tries to flick it but gets a soft leading edge towards the cover fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Haris Rauf to David Miller, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle and leg, Heinrich Klaasen looks to play it on the off side but miscues it through backward square leg for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Haris Rauf to Heinrich Klaasen, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it outside off, David Miller guides it to short third for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Haris Rauf to David Miller, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot! Fuller one, on off, David Miller stays in his crease and drives it magnificently through mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Haris Rauf to David Miller, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Haris Rauf comes into the attack as the first change, replacing Shaheen Afridi.
Flighted up, on off, angling in a shade. Heinrich Klaasen stays in his crease and punches it to the cover fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Abrar Ahmed to Heinrich Klaasen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short, on off, Heinrich Klaasen hangs back and blocks it solidly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Abrar Ahmed to Heinrich Klaasen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The captain Heinrich Klaasen walks in with his side in early trouble. A slip in place for Klaasen.

OUT! TIMBER! Abrar Ahmed gets his second! A googly from Abrar Ahmed, it landed around middle and turned back in. Reeza Hendricks was on the leg stump as he tried to cut it but missed it completely. He plays it off the back foot to a delivery he should have been on the front foot. He fails to pick the googly and the ball sneaks past the inside edge to leave the stumps in a mess. South Africa continue to crumble.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Abrar Ahmed to Reeza Hendricks, OUT! b Abrar Ahmed.

Commentary.Commentary: Past the edge! Looped up outside off, Reeza Hendricks wafts at it and is beaten all ends up!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Abrar Ahmed to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short, around off, David Miller tucks it to mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Abrar Ahmed to David Miller, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, on off, Reeza Hendricks drags it over mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Abrar Ahmed to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitched, on off, Reeza Hendricks hangs back and turns it towards mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, on off, David Miller punches it towards mid off. Haris Rauf dives to his right and stops a possible boundary. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shaheen Afridi to David Miller, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: That's a tight leave! On a length and outside off, it nips in. David Miller reads it well and leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to David Miller, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length, on off, David Miller hangs back and blocks it to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shaheen Afridi to David Miller, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! What a good shot this is! On a length and outside off, David Miller is severe onto it as he cracks a drive through the cover region to find the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shaheen Afridi to David Miller, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Well played! Goes fuller and on middle and leg, David Miller makes a good connection and pumps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to David Miller, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Whipped to the cow-corner boundary! Short, on off, Reeza Hendricks holds onto a stable base and lets his bottom hand take over. Gets it over the fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Abrar Ahmed to Reeza Hendricks, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short, on off, Reeza Hendricks punches it to the cover fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Abrar Ahmed to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller again, on middle, David Miller flicks it along the floor through mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Abrar Ahmed to David Miller, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Fullish ball, pushing it down leg, David Miller looks to flick it but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Abrar Ahmed to David Miller, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: David Miller is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Quicker one has done the trick here. Abrar Ahmed delivers it on a shortish length outside off,  Matthew Breetzke winds up for another big shot through the line but mistimes it completely. The ball carries towards Saim Ayub at backward point who makes no mistake. A short stay for Matthew Breetzke. Abrar folds his arms and with a bit of head nod gives a send-off to Breetzke.
Commentary.Howout: c Saim Ayub b Abrar Ahmed
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Abrar Ahmed to Matthew Breetzke, OUT! c Saim Ayub b Abrar Ahmed.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Right out of the screws! Half-tracker outside off that sits up to be hit. Matthew Breetzke winds up and clatters it over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Abrar Ahmed to Matthew Breetzke, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Short, angling in, Matthew Breetzke stays in his crease and blocks it to short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Abrar Ahmed to Matthew Breetzke, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be spin in the form of Abrar Ahmed from the other end.
What an over from Shaheen Afridi! This is streaky again. Length, on off, Matthew Breetzke looks to block it but edges it past the slip fielder for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Breetzke, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Too full again, on off, Reeza Hendricks drills it towards cover where Tayyab Tahir dives to his right to save a certain boundary. Just a single off it then.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitched, on off, Matthew Breetzke drives it to extra cover for one. He gets off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Breetzke, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Matthew Breetzke walks in at number 3.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Shaheen Afridi strikes as Rassie van der Dussen departs for a golden duck! Goes fuller this time, outside off, Rassie van der Dussen looks to fetch it from outside off but gets a thick inside edge. The ball goes on to hit the off pole. A fine start from Pakistan!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Rassie van der Dussen, OUT! b Shaheen Afridi.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh! Length again, outside off, Reeza Hendricks looks to block it again but gets squared up as the ball goes away. Miscues it through backward point for one. What a start from Shaheen Afridi! Something seems to be brewing here!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Straight on the money! Shaheen starts with a length ball, on leg and it jags back in. Reeza Hendricks looks to block it but wears it on his pads. A loud appeal but turned down. Perhaps missing leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Time to get going in the series opener. Overcast skies greet the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. Mohammad Rizwan and his men break from the huddle to take their respective positions in the field. Rassie van der Dussen and Reeza Hendricks are the two openers for South Africa. Shaheen Afridi will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Pakistan. A solitary slip in place. Here we go!
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Rizwan (C/WK), Babar Azam, Saim Ayub, Usman Khan, Tayyab Tahir, Irfan Khan, Abbas Afridi, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Sufiyan Muqeem, Abrar Ahmed.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Rassie van der Dussen, Reeza Hendricks, Matthew Breetzke, David Miller, Heinrich Klaasen (C/WK), Donovan Ferreira, George Linde, Andile Simelane, Nqabayomzi Peter, Kwena Maphaka, Ottneil Baartman.
TOSS - South Africa have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Historically, Pakistan have had the upper hand in T20Is between these two teams, including a dominant 3-1 series win on South African soil back in 2021. South Africa will be keen to turn the tables and secure their first series in T20Is over Pakistan since 2019. So, sit back, relax, and get ready for an exciting match between two top cricketing nations. Stick around for the toss and team news.

On the other hand, Pakistan enter the series on the back of a white-ball adventure in Zimbabwe, and they will be eager to carry that momentum forward. Skipper Mohammad Rizwan returns, as does Babar Azam, and a lot will rest on the shoulders of this experienced duo. Saim Ayub, in the early stages of his T20I career, has begun well, and he will be keen to excel here. The playing XI announced earlier in the day boasts of a formidable pace trio of Haris Rauf, Shaheen Afridi, and Abbas Afridi, with Sufiyan Muqeem and Abrar Ahmed handling the spin bowling duties.

South Africa enter this series with some fresh changes in their T20I squad. The Proteas will be without some key players for the T20I leg, including the likes of Aiden Markram, Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen, and Keshav Maharaj, all of whom were involved in the recently concluded Test series against Sri Lanka. In Markram's absence, Heinrich Klaasen will take over the reins. Despite these absences, the South African batting lineup remains potent, with experienced campaigners like Reeza Hendricks, David Miller, and Rassie van der Dussen. The spin department will be manned by the likes of Tabraiz Shamsi and George Linde, though Shamsi's availability for this game is uncertain due to his participation in the recently concluded Global Super League. The pace attack will be led by Anrich Nortje, and it also features exciting names like Kwena Maphaka and Ottneil Baartman.

Hello and welcome to the first T20I of the three-match series between South Africa and Pakistan at Kingsmead in Durban. Cricket fans around the world are in for a thrilling ride as these two cricketing giants lock horns in what promises to be an exciting clash to kick off this multi-format series. The series will feature three T20Is, three ODIs, and two Tests, adding another layer of intensity to the non-stop cricket calendar that has become a hallmark of modern-day international cricket.
... MATCH DAY ...

Modern cricket has evolved into a non-stop spectacle, treating fans to endless action across the globe. Adding to this perpetual cricket calendar, South Africa is set to host Pakistan in an exciting multi-format series, spanning T20Is, ODIs, and Tests. The tour begins at Durban's historic Kingsmead ground with the first of three T20Is, before moving on to three ODIs and two Test matches. The Proteas T20I squad sees some notable changes, with Heinrich Klaasen taking the captaincy reins in place of Aiden Markram, who's focused on his Test captain duties. Several key players - Tristan Stubbs, Marco Jansen, Kagiso Rabada, and Keshav Maharaj - will sit out the T20Is following their involvement in the recent Test series against Sri Lanka, though they're scheduled to return for the ODI leg. The spin department will be handled by a trio comprising Tabraiz Shamsi, Nqabayomzi Peter, and George Linde. The pace bowling responsibilities fall to young talents Kwena Maphaka, Andile Simelane, and Ottneil Baartman, with Patrick Kruger providing an additional all-round option. Despite some absences, the batting lineup remains formidable, featuring experienced campaigners like Reeza Hendricks, Rassie van der Dussen, and David Miller alongside captain Klaasen. Pakistan enters the series riding high on confidence following their successful white-ball campaign in Zimbabwe. The squad, led by the dynamic Mohammad Rizwan, who'll also don the keeping gloves, presents a formidable unit on paper. In the batting department, all eyes will be on Babar Azam, despite his recent form concerns. The former captain remains a crucial figure in the top order, supported by emerging talents Saim Ayub and Usman Khan. The squad has been refreshed with new faces, including Omair Yousuf and Tayyab Tahir, while all-rounder Salman Agha adds depth to the lineup. The bowling arsenal looks particularly threatening with the pace trio of Haris Rauf, Shaheen Shah Afridi, and Mohammad Abbas. The spin contingent features Abrar Ahmed and Salman Agha as the primary options, with Sufiyan Muqeem providing additional support. Pakistan carries a psychological advantage in this series, having historically dominated South Africa in T20Is. They'll draw particular confidence from their previous tour in 2021, where they secured a convincing 3-1 series victory on South African soil. The last South Africa won a series against Pakistan was back in 2018/19 when Faf du Plessis used to lead the pack. So, it’s been quite a wait for them to defeat Pakistan, that too, on their home soil. However, if we look at their overall head-to-head clashes, it shows how closely contested these two teams have been, with Pakistan having a thin edge over the South Africans by 12-10. Will the Proteas pack a punch this time, or can Pakistan maintain their winning streak? Whatever the result is, this series will be a sure-shot box-office entertainer.
